title: Low and high in Celsius
statement:
Turn the low and the high temperature from Fahrenheit into Celsius.

The input has `low_f` and `high_f`. Give an object with `low` and `high` in Celsius. To convert, take 32 away, then times 5, then divide by 9. Write the conversion once as `def to_c: ...;` and use `to_c` for both fields.

title: Test run summary
statement:
Count the tests that passed, the tests that failed and the tests that were slow.

The input is an array of tests. Each test has a `status` and a time `ms`. A slow test has `ms` over 1000. Give an object with the counts `passed`, `failed` and `slow`. Start with `def count(f): map(select(f)) | length;`. Then call it three times, for example `count(.status == "passed")`.
reference:
def count(f): map(select(f)) | length;
{passed: count(.status == "passed"), failed: count(.status == "failed"), slow: count(.ms > 1000)}

title: Song lengths
statement:
Give the length of the longest song and the length of the whole album, in seconds.

The input is an array of songs. Each song has a `length` as text like `"3:05"`: minutes, a colon, then seconds. Give an object with `longest` and `total`, both as numbers of seconds. Write a filter `def secs: ...;` that turns one length text into seconds. Use `split(":")` and `tonumber` in it. Then use `secs` for both fields.
reference:
def secs: split(":") | (.[0] | tonumber) * 60 + (.[1] | tonumber);
{longest: (map(.length | secs) | max), total: (map(.length | secs) | add)}
